title: Escape the Backrooms
provenance: Reported by verylovestars (highball-db#296 and highball-db#299, 2026-10-03), Apple M4 Pro, macOS 27.0.1, Highball 0.9.39, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r11, D3DMetal as the environment's mode with a winhttp=n DLL override, recipes steam and vcrun2022, rated 5 of 5 after 5 minutes and again after 272 minutes (over 60 fps on average, the reporter added on 2026-10-14) (the second report's renderer field says DXMT while its environment line says D3DMetal, this row goes by the environment). A third report by WaterWANG-1014 (highball-db#302, 2026-10-04), Apple M4 Max, macOS 15.8, Highball 0.10.2, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r17, D3DMetal with AVX advertised and D3DM_SUPPORT_DXR=0, recipes steam, hogwarts-legacy and vcrun2022, rated 5 of 5 after 2 minutes. Not verified by the maintainer. Ces4rr-b (highball-db#723, 2026-10-27), Apple M5, macOS 27.0.1, Highball 0.10.22, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r28, D3DMetal by the report (the environment's mode line says DXMT), msync, rated 5 of 5 after 2 minutes.
notes: An Unreal Engine game, Direct3D 11 or 12 by its store page. Reported perfect three times on D3DMetal, the longest a four and a half hour session on an M4 Pro on the default engine r11, and a two-minute look on an M4 Max on macOS 15.8 with engine r17. Which of the game's two Direct3D paths ran under D3DMetal is not known and nobody tried DXMT, so the mode here is the one that worked rather than a comparison. The first reporter's winhttp override and the third reporter's AVX and D3DM_SUPPORT_DXR settings were in place in the working runs, whether any of them is needed is not known, and the hogwarts-legacy recipe in that environment belongs to another game. No frame rate was given and nothing was measured here.
